analysis:
The only changed file is scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, a CI route-test script, so it is outside the provider and coordinator runtime trust boundaries in the threat model. I found no change to provider keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, prefix-cache crypto, or any coordinator-to-provider path (TB-002, TB-011, T-041 and related IDs).

The diff removes the BUILT/built() helper, so build lanes now use requested(component) instead of a push-skip refresh. It adds a cluster_gpu component for the GPU shard lanes. It also changes the watchdog and hourly test assertions around the end of the file, and the head side shifts the line numbers.

The CI controls the tests assert are unchanged or still pinned:
- The router job has empty permissions and no secrets or checkout.
- Forks never contact the plane.
- Plain HTTP is rejected.
- Only an exact label array is accepted.
- Release and credentialed workflows keep literal blacksmith runners.
- Routed jobs are read-only.

One limit on coverage: the head text I saw ends at line 563, so the head side of the later tests (the watchdog and hourly tests, shifted to roughly lines 1025-1078) was not directly visible. I judged those only from the base text and the patch ranges. The actual workflow files (provider-plan.yml, provider-tests.yml, darkbloom-route.yml) were not supplied, so I cannot confirm that the cluster_gpu component exists in the workflows or that the test and workflow edits stay consistent. That is a test-integrity question, not a demonstrated security regression. Integration should check that the workflow changes keep the read-only permissions and literal-runner invariants these tests enforce.
